summary: Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a Diplôme at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he served as a research advisor in Tibetan Studies.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Honjo studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Kobe Women's University (1989–2004) and Bukkyo University (1980; 2004; 2010; professor 2014), with additional appointments attested at Otani University and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 2000 to 2024.

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto at Komazawa University, where he also spent his main career as a lecturer from 1971 and professor from 2001.

A historian of Japan, Amino studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1947 to 1953. His major academic appointments included posts at Nagoya University (~1973–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1993).

Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and holding leadership roles at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

A specialist in Buddhist studies, Sakurai studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). His career includes positions as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Yoshihiro Hayashi is attested in 2009 as a professor at Ritsumeikan University and as a part-time lecturer at Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He spent his career at Taisho University, where he served as professor (attested 1991–1999) and was appointed president in 2001.

Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He held posts at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He held an attested post at Otani University in 2013 and is affiliated with the Otani Academic Society as of 2026.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Yoshimi Nozawa is attested in 2026 as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

A scholar of Japanese history, Kimoto studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He served as associate professor at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College, president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakade was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga at Kyoto University (~1953–1961) and held a long-term academic post at Kansai University from circa 1978 to 2004.

Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, later serving as associate professor (1948) and professor (1959–1976), followed by a professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (~1978–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a scholar in Sinology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1956–1958), serving as a library-track research assistant at Kyoto University from circa 1951 to 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued his training under teachers Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1910 and held a major academic post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1946.

A Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Imaeda studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Shoju Inaba. He held posts at CNRS, National Library of Bhutan, and Kyoto University.

Tamura was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University (1965–1972), the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1980–1989).
